question: For years, the neighbourhood association of Los Manchegos, a district of San Vicent del Raspeig (Alicante), has been complaining about the presence of asbestos in the former Levante fibre cement factory, between the building debris and the undergrowth.

The Commission, through various proposals, has called on all EU institutions and Member States to speed up their action towards an asbestos-free European Union for current and future generations. In June 2023, the EU amended its rules to reduce the maximum asbestos exposure limits, established due to the carcinogenic risk associated with the substance. 1.
What measures will the Commission take to ensure that Member States oblige the competent authorities to speed up the removal of this highly carcinogenic substance in cities?

Does the Commission intend to ask for information and investigate the above case, given the inaction of the local government and the regional Ministry of the Environment itself and their refusal to recognise the serious problems faced by local residents in order to ensure compliance with EU rules?
Does the Commission not consider it necessary to approve structural funds to finance the removal of asbestos and protect public health?
answer: The Commission has long recognised the danger of asbestos and has worked for the protection of people and the environment.

In September 2022, the Commission presented a communication on working towards an asbestos-free futur e (1) where it announced to put forward a new legislative proposal for a revision of the 2009 Directive on the protection of workers from the risk of exposure to asbestos (2) , adopted on 22 November 2023 (3), (4).
The Waste Framework Directive (5) requires Member States to take the necessary measures to ensure that waste management is carried out without endangering human health, nor the environment.

The Commission is not aware of the case mentioned in the written question and would like to highlight that the recently revised Spanish Waste Law (6) requires municipalities, within a year of entry into force of the law, to make an inventory of asbestos containing sites and installations and to provide a calendar for its removal (7).

As regards individual cases of possible incorrect application not raising systematic failure to comply with EU law, the national administrative and judicial bodies are better placed to ensure that EU legislation is respected and have the necessary territorial proximity to assess situations such as the one described by the Honourable Member.

However, the Commission will monitor the situation and may decide to take action. Structural funds are implemented under shared management between the Commission and Member States. The Member States make the proposal for the use of the funds and select the individual projects that receive support.

The reduction of all form of pollution is eligible for support from the European Regional Development Fund, under the specific conditions of the fund’s regulation (8) and of the programme approved by the Commission (9).

Regulation (EU) 2021/1058 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 24 June 2021 on the European Regional Development Fund and on the Cohesion Fund. Mainly the soil decontamination and remediation, rehabilitation of industrial sites and contaminated land, including old and illegal landfill sites.
